title: Stabilize incident paging via ephemeral spike filters and adaptive quiet windows
creator: Aisha Chen
description: After the 2025-02-12 capacity regression, oncall saw a 3x increase in pages driven by short-lived token-burst SLO spikes that resolved within 2-4 minutes. This ticket implements short-window spike suppression and smarter quiet windows to avoid transient-induced paging while preserving real degradation signals.
background: Incident reference: incident-2025-02-12-capacity-regression (postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.company/postmortems/incident-2025-02-12). Symptoms: bursty 5xxs from overloaded GPU pools, proportional burn-rate alerts firing across 4 services, multiple successive pages for the same underlying regression. Previous mitigations (manual mute and scale-up) worked but caused oncall fatigue and delayed root-cause work.
proposed_solution: 1) Ephemeral spike filters: detect minute-scale spikes (<= 5 minutes) and suppress paging while emitting a lower-severity internal incident log. 2) Adaptive quiet windows: lengthen quiet windows when consecutive pages are correlated to same fingerprinted root cause; shorten when independent. 3) Sliding-quantile thresholds: compute thresholds over decaying window to avoid reacting to transient distribution shifts. 4) Probe-based canary suppression: run a low-rate synthetic probe to confirm user-impacting regressions before paging. 5) Impact-weighted escalation: tie pagering to customer-impact score, not raw burn magnitude.

2025-02-20 - Priya Kapoor: Design review notes - prefer request-path + model-version fingerprinting over IP-based grouping to avoid noise from load-balancer churn.

2025-02-25 - Diego Morales: Prototype unit tests passing for spike filter. Basic metric emitted 'suppression_decisions' with tags. Observed one false-suppress in staging tied to a multi-minute degradation; will tune to require sustained delta before suppression.
2025-03-01 - Marcus Lee: Canary probe implemented; latency overhead negligible. Suggest gating pages on probe-fail for P1 routes only during first two rollout phases.
